page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 series. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. It comes provisioned with 128 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

A key differentiator for the D32ds_v4 is the integration of 1288 GB of high-speed local SSD storage alongside premium remote storage capability. Benchmark evaluations place the instance consistently within the middle 50% across compute and memory workloads. The instance registered a multi-core score of 10,167 in Geekbench and 29,822.96 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 27,517.37. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 107.43 GB/sec, while write operations reached 48.06 GB/sec.

In operational benchmarks, the instance sustained 27.94 million operations per second during Redis SET testing and delivered a static web serving throughput of 21.18 GB/sec. Software compilation via Clang scored 22,155 on Geekbench. Single-threaded gzip compression performance trended weaker, ranking in the bottom 25% at 23.52 GB/sec. Small-scale CPU-based machine learning inference is viable, managing 57.9 prompt processing tokens per second on 7B parameter models, though processing speeds drop significantly on larger models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of direct local NVMe SSD storage eliminates secondary storage spend for temporary scratch data, caching tiers, and swap space. Given its balanced compute, memory footprint, and local disk volume, the D32ds_v4 fits enterprise web applications, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, relational database backends, intermediate ETL tasks, and multi-threaded CI/CD compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it includes 128 GB of RAM and 1288 GB of local SSD scratch storage. Benchmark performance is balanced across mainstream enterprise tests, scoring 10,167 on multi-core Geekbench, 27,517.37 on PassMark CPU, and handling 27.94 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth scales up to 107.43 GB/sec for uncached reads. The absence of a dedicated GPU limits intensive deep learning inference, and single-threaded compression performance sits in the lower quartile. Combining balanced memory density with expansive high-speed temporary storage, this instance is well matched for relational databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise application serving, and multi-stage CI/CD compilation pipelines.
